entries.odia: କଣ୍ଟାଫିରିକି, ଏତେ ଗୁଣ ବୋଲି ଜାଣିଥିଲି କି ବେଳସୁଁ ନ କହିଲୁ ଫୁଲପରା କରି ଟେକି ଧରିଥିଲୁ କଚାଡ଼ି ପକେଇଲୁ
entries.title: Raised like a flower, then dropped
entries.literal_meaning: Thorny phiriki, did I know you had such qualities? Why did you not tell me in time? You held me up like a flower, then flung me down.
entries.explanation: The voice turns on someone who first treated the speaker tenderly and then hurtfully reversed that treatment. “Such qualities” can be heard as an ironic compliment: the ending reveals why the earlier admiration has soured. The linked dictionary entry identifies phiriki as a thorny plant; the flower and the thorn therefore offer a sharp contrast without requiring a story about a particular person. The main entry supplies the words but no separate account of their occasion. Our conversational reading is a reproach for praise or support followed by abrupt rejection, not proof of a named betrayal or romance.
entries.meaning_odia: ଆଗରୁ ଫୁଲ ପରି ଟେକି ଧରିଲ, ପରେ କଚାଡ଼ି ପକାଇଲ—ଏହି ଓଲଟା ଆଚରଣକୁ ଧରି ବକ୍ତା ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରୁଛନ୍ତି। ଏତେ ଗୁଣ ଥିଲା ବୋଲି କହିବାଟି ଏଠାରେ ପ୍ରଶଂସାର ଓଲଟା ସ୍ୱରରେ ଶୁଣାଯାଇପାରେ। ଅଭିଧାନର ସଂଯୁକ୍ତ ପିରିକ ଶବ୍ଦରେ କଣ୍ଟାଯୁକ୍ତ ଗଛର କଥା ଅଛି; ଫୁଲ ପରି ଆଦର ଓ କଣ୍ଟାର ଖୋଚା ଏହି ପାଠରେ ପାଖାପାଖି ଆସେ। ପ୍ରଥମେ ଭରସା ବା ପ୍ରଶଂସା ଦେଇ ପରେ ହଠାତ୍ ଦୂରେଇଦେବାକୁ ଏହି କଥାରେ ଅଭିଯୋଗ କରିହୁଏ। କୌଣସି ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ପ୍ରେମକାହାଣୀ ବା ଘଟଣାକୁ ଏହାର ମୂଳ ବୋଲି ଉତ୍ସ କହେନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: A reproach turns earlier praise into irony when tender support ends in abrupt rejection.
entries.odia_summary: ଆଗରୁ ଆଦର କରି ପରେ ଦୂରେଇଦେଲେ ପ୍ରଶଂସାର ସ୍ୱର ଅଭିଯୋଗରେ ବଦଳିଯାଏ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A theatre group warmly praises a volunteer’s idea and asks them to prepare it. At the next meeting, the same people dismiss it without explanation. The volunteer quotes the saying to point out that sudden reversal. The theatre setting is invented, not the source’s occasion.
entries.cultural_context: The source labels this a saying; its linked lexical entry supplies only the thorny-plant meaning. No species identification, medicinal property, actual physical assault or fixed romantic relationship is claimed. Flower/thorn contrast and the modern conversational application are editorial readings.

entries.odia: କାଣି କଉଡ଼ି ପିତା ତାଳ, ୟାକୁ ଦେଉଥିବ ରାତ୍ରିକାଳ
entries.title: Passing it on after dark
entries.literal_meaning: A worthless cowrie, a bitter palm fruit—give these at night.
entries.explanation: Two disappointing things are paired with a convenient hour for giving: darkness. The dictionary identifies the cowrie as tiny or broken and, in the latter sense, worthless shell money. The saying itself gives no explanatory story. One possible reading is a dry joke about passing on something poor when its defects may be harder to notice. The surface instruction need not become our advice: quoted critically, it can expose the attempt to make a bad offering pass for a good one. We do not infer who receives them, or a custom that required such giving.
entries.meaning_odia: କାଣି କଉଡ଼ି ଓ ପିତା ତାଳ—ଦୁଇଟି ଅପସନ୍ଦ ହେବା ଭଳି ଜିନିଷ ସାଙ୍ଗରେ ଦେବାର ସମୟ ରଖାଯାଇଛି ରାତି। ଅଭିଧାନ କଉଡ଼ିଟିକୁ ଛୋଟ ବା ଭଙ୍ଗା, ଆଉ ଭଙ୍ଗା ଅର୍ଥରେ ମୂଲ୍ୟହୀନ ବୋଲି କହିଛି। ଅନ୍ଧାରରେ ଦୋଷ ଭଲକରି ଦେଖାନଯିବାର ସୁଯୋଗ ନେଇ ଖରାପ ଜିନିଷ ଚଳାଇଦେବାର ଶୁଖିଲା ଥଟ୍ଟା ଭାବେ ଏହାକୁ ପଢ଼ିହୁଏ। ଏହା ଆମର ପ୍ରୟୋଗମୂଳକ ପାଠ; ଉତ୍ସ ଅଲଗା ଘଟଣା ବା ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଦେଇନାହିଁ। କାହାର ଏମିତି ଚାଲାକିକୁ ଧରି କଥାଟି କୁହାଯାଇପାରେ, ସେହି ଚାଲାକି କରିବାକୁ ପରାମର୍ଶ ଦେବା ପାଇଁ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: One possible reading is a dry joke about passing on something poor under cover of darkness.
entries.odia_summary: ଖରାପ ଜିନିଷକୁ ଅନ୍ଧାରରେ ଚଳାଇଦେବାର ଚାଲାକି ଉପରେ ଏକ ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ କଟାକ୍ଷ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A friend notices that a damaged second-hand lamp is being shown to a buyer only in a dim corner. They quote the saying and ask that the lamp be brought into the light before anyone decides. This modern scene is an editorial use, not a documented trading custom.
entries.cultural_context: The cowrie is a historical money image in the source gloss. The darkness/deception interpretation is not separately defined there and remains an editorial reading. No specific recipient, ritual, trade practice or origin is supplied. The fruit wording is retained without a botanical or dietary claim.

entries.title: A twig among ornaments
entries.literal_meaning: Among the ornaments, a neem twig has a place.
entries.explanation: The line puts a small ordinary twig among things normally valued for adornment. A separate dictionary entry explains that a piece of neem twig could occupy an ear or nose piercing when an ornament was absent. That historical description makes the juxtaposition less random: the twig stands in the place an ornament would otherwise occupy. It does not, by itself, settle whether every speaker intends affection, modest pride or a dismissive comparison. One editorial application is to notice an unassuming substitute that serves a purpose among more impressive things. The source’s old bodily practice is context, not a recommendation to reproduce it.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଳଙ୍କାରମାନଙ୍କ ଭିତରେ ସାଧାରଣ ନିମକାଠିର ମଧ୍ୟ ସ୍ଥାନ ଅଛି—ଏହି ପାଖାପାଖି ରଖିବାଟି କଥାର ଚମକ। ଅନ୍ୟ ଏକ ଅଭିଧାନ ଶବ୍ଦରେ ଅଳଙ୍କାର ନଥିଲେ କାନ ବା ନାକର ଫୋଡ଼ରେ ଛୋଟ ନିମକାଠି ରଖାଯିବାର ପୁରୁଣା ବ୍ୟବହାର ବର୍ଣ୍ଣିତ ଅଛି। ସେହି ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନା ଧରିଲେ କାଠିଟି କାହିଁକି ଅଳଙ୍କାର ପାଖରେ ଆସିଲା, ବୁଝିହୁଏ। ତେବେ କଥାଟିରେ ଆଦର, ନିଜ ସାଧାରଣତାକୁ ନେଇ ହସ, ନା ତାଚ୍ଛଲ୍ୟ—ସବୁ ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ପାଇଁ ଏକ ସ୍ୱର ଉତ୍ସ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ କରେନାହିଁ। ଆଡ଼ମ୍ବର ଭିତରେ କାମରେ ଲାଗୁଥିବା ସାଧାରଣ ବଦଳି ଜିନିଷକୁ ଚିହ୍ନିବା ଏହାର ଗୋଟିଏ ପ୍ରୟୋଗମୂଳକ ପାଠ।
entries.english_summary: An ordinary twig beside ornaments suggests a place for an unassuming substitute, though tone depends on use.
entries.odia_summary: ଅଳଙ୍କାର ପାଖରେ ନିମକାଠି—ସାଧାରଣ ବଦଳି ଜିନିଷର ସ୍ଥାନ ଦେଖାଇବାର ଗୋଟିଏ ଚିତ୍ର।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: At a music rehearsal, several people arrive with polished music stands. One singer uses a plain homemade book support and jokingly quotes the line about the twig among ornaments. The comparison concerns the modest substitute, not the singer’s worth. This is an editorial application, not a sourced musical tradition.
entries.cultural_context: 88757 supplies a related variant and supplementary lexical context in the same dictionary lineage, not independent corroboration. It includes a longer variant with the unresolved digital word ନୀକରେ; that variant is preserved in the capture but not silently normalized or treated as a second saying. No piercing method, medical safety claim or named community practice is recommended.
